clue.text: Not liable to change horses

definitions.meaning: a building where horses are kept, or a group of racehorses under one trainer

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to switch mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady resists change, and the word is also the noun for a yard housing horses.

clue.text: Saw part, one of a set

definitions.meaning: one of the cutting points along a saw blade
a single member of a set of teeth, as in dentures

explanation.surface: A piece of a saw that belongs to a matching set.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw blade has a row of sharp points, and each of those, like each item in a mouthful of dentures, is a cusp-like peg.

clue.text: Weapon for Xanthippe

definitions.meaning: a broad-headed axe used in war
Socrates' wife, proverbial as a scolding, domineering woman

explanation.surface: Choosing an arm for an ancient Greek woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Xanthippe, wife of Socrates, is the classic shrew, so she is an example of the formidable woman the term also names.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is both a medieval war axe and slang for a fierce, overbearing woman such as Socrates' wife.

clue.text: Get free points — and another point

parts.note: E (east) is a compass point
S (south) is another compass point
a cape is a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A scorer is told to collect bonus points and then one more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' gives two compass letters, E and S; the 'point' that follows is a geographical headland.
explanation.definitionFit: To get free is to break out or flee from confinement.

clue.text: Save Bobby Shafto, for example

definitions.meaning: to put money aside secretly for later
in the nursery rhyme Bobby Shafto has gone to sea, so he is a sailor (salt) who is away

explanation.surface: Rescue the hero of an old nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby Shafto's gone to sea' is a traditional English nursery rhyme; a SALT is an old sailor, and he is AWAY at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash money for the future is to hoard it; read literally the phrase is a sailor absent at sea.

clue.text: Simple, honest and progressive

parts.note: an honest person is straight, not crooked
progressive means moving ahead, forward-looking

explanation.surface: A description of an admirable person: uncomplicated, truthful and modern in outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The three adjectives look like a list of virtues; the first is the definition and the other two build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncomplicated and easy to follow is described as direct and plain.

clue.text: Gap in law seen through in Old Bailey

definitions.meaning: an ambiguity or omission that lets someone evade a rule
a narrow slit in a castle wall, the bailey being a castle's outer wall, through which archers looked and shot

explanation.surface: A legal weakness exposed in London's central criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court, which the surface relies on; but a bailey is also a castle's outer wall, pierced by slits for archers.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal escape route is a gap in the rules, and the same word names an arrow slit in a fortified wall.

clue.text: Frighten in jolly style?

parts.note: together with 'style', 'in ... style' renders the French a la, meaning in the manner of
a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A question of whether one can scare someone in a cheerful way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in jolly style' means 'à la Royal Marine': 'in ... style' gives A LA and 'jolly', not an adjective here, is a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: To scare someone is to startle or panic them.

clue.text: Character sometimes coming between father and son

definitions.text: Character sometimes coming between father and son

parts.words: Character sometimes coming between father and son
parts.note: a printed symbol, the and-sign, placed between the names in a firm's title such as Smith & Son

explanation.surface: Someone whose personality causes friction between a dad and his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person causing a family rift, but it is a typographical character, as in 'Dombey & Son'.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol for 'and' sits between words in business names like 'X & Son'.

clue.text: Unusually clean motor at end of rally

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the two words that follow set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A car that has been washed arrives at the finish of a motor rally.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monte Carlo Rally famously finishes in Monaco, so the place is the 'end of rally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous motor rally finishes in the Monaco resort town that gives it its name.

clue.text: Head off insects, venomous creatures

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the word for insects is cut away

parts.note: wasps are stinging insects

explanation.surface: An instruction to block the advance of insects and poisonous animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a verb meaning intercept, but it removes the first letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: Small poisonous snakes, such as the Egyptian cobra, are venomous creatures.

clue.text: King of Spain, sanctimonious after battle

parts.note: Philip is the name of several Spanish kings, such as Philip II
pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A Spanish monarch behaving self-righteously after a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is only a link: the definition, the battle of 42 BC in Macedonia, follows the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian city gave its name to the 42 BC battle where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius.

clue.text: Man's brother is not out, apparently

indicators.note: the brother is placed within, so 'is' (here, is in) puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: not out is at home, in the cricket sense the batsman is 'in'

explanation.surface: A man's sibling is apparently staying in.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish for 'man', used in American slang. 'not out' is HOME, and BR (brother) is in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a fellow, borrowed into American slang, means a guy.

clue.text: Plan or model that's detailed, so to speak

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word for model loses its final letter

parts.note: a model is an ideal, a perfect example

explanation.surface: A scheme or prototype that has been worked out in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means 'with its tail removed', hence 'so to speak', taking the L off IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a notion or scheme of what to do.

clue.text: Severe on Scot after eccentric's upset

indicators.note: after puts the second pieces behind the first
in a down clue, upset means the word for eccentric is turned upside down

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Harsh treatment of a Scotsman after an odd person is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is an eccentric; 'upset' suits a down clue, where the word reads upwards. 'after' puts that turned piece before ON and the Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Athenian lawgiver Draco, whose laws were notoriously harsh, so excessively strict.

clue.text: Port for the abbot, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a ferry port in Anglesey, north Wales
an abbot is the sacred chief of a monastery, a pious leader

explanation.surface: A drink offered to the head of the monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink; it is the Welsh ferry port for Ireland. An abbot is a 'holy head'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglesey harbour is a ferry terminal, and read in two words it describes a sacred leader such as an abbot.

clue.text: Firm control needed in family

parts.note: a house is a business firm, as in a publishing house
to have a hold over something is to control it

explanation.surface: A domestic situation where strict discipline is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone living under one roof, a family and its dependants, forms a domestic unit.

clue.text: Unsophisticated detective left out witticism

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed from the detective

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes is the fictional detective
a pun is a joke on words, a witticism

explanation.surface: A naive investigator omitted a clever remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from HOLMES, leaving HOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth woven at home is plain and simple, so the word means homely and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Becomes successful, and departs

definitions.meaning: suddenly becomes popular, like a product selling fast
leaves, as a plane leaves the ground

explanation.surface: Someone rises to fame and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that soars succeeds rapidly, and an aircraft leaving the runway departs.

clue.text: Open up ruin

explanation.surface: An order to open a ruined building.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten is to open, and to be someone's downfall is to wreck them.

clue.text: Completely exhausted, with everyone on strike

definitions.meaning: having used every last bit of effort
a strike in which all workers walk out

explanation.surface: Worn out because the whole workforce has downed tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximum effort leaves one spent, and a total walkout has every worker striking.

clue.text: Pair left in carriage for two

indicators.note: in places the letter for left within the carriage

parts.note: a coupe is a closed horse-drawn carriage seating two

explanation.surface: Two people abandoned in a two-seater vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of something, or two partners, make a duo.

clue.text: Singularly low-priced fruit

parts.note: P stands for a penny, the lowest price
each means individually, taken singly

explanation.surface: An extraordinarily cheap piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'a penny apiece': P (penny) then EACH, though the clue gives 'Singularly' first.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, downy stone fruit is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Ever worked with oils? Outstanding works result

indicators.note: worked means the letters of the neighbouring words are fashioned into a new shape

explanation.surface: A question about whether an artist painted in oils, with standout pieces resulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means projecting: these are sculptures in relief, standing out from the background.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief carvings project from their surface, so they are literally standing out.

clue.text: Like Eliza in this fur?

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion drops her aitches, so a warmer coat would be, in her voice, missing its first letter; the coat is an aquatic mammal's pelt

explanation.surface: Asking how a Cockney flower girl would feel in a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle, Shaw's Cockney flower girl, drops her h's: in this fur she'd be 'hotter', said ''otter'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of the river mammal is a fur, and an h-dropping speaker says 'hotter' this way.

clue.text: African country half-switched capital city

indicators.note: half-switched says the two halves of the country's name change places

parts.note: Mali is a West African country

explanation.surface: An African state has partly moved its seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: MA and LI change places to give the capital of Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Provider of music in key when in operation, perhaps

indicators.note: when in places the key letter within the rearranged word
perhaps signals the word operation given in some other arrangement

parts.note: F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Something that plays tunes in tune when it is running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key when in operation' suggests a piece being played; 'perhaps' scrambles the nine letters of 'operation' and 'when in' sets the key letter F among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the keyboard instrument, which provides music.

clue.text: Some discussion, then? Oddly, without any

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that, strangely, there is no debate at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'discussion' earlier in the clue: passed without any discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal approved by assent, with no debate, goes through by agreement without discussion.

clue.text: Line starting in Wales that could go into' Stroud

indicators.note: could go into signals the town's letters can be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A railway route beginning in Wales that might run into a Gloucestershire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroud is a Gloucestershire town; the 'line' is a royal dynasty, which began with Welsh-born Henry VII.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal dynasty founded by Henry VII, of Welsh descent, is a line of monarchs.
